playerText.title: Chapter 2: False Colors
playerText.summary: Answer the accusation against the Breckenridge, protect the wounded, and establish a credible path forward.

Aegis Two was attacked by a vessel presenting as the U.S.S. Breckenridge. Three patrol officers are injured, the real ship was at the convoy site, and Starfleet-controlled records alone cannot settle the dispute.
Compact leaders require independently credible verification, while a demand for broad system access conflicts with Starfleet's duty to protect dangerous command-authentication architecture.

Preserved non-Starfleet records and the Breckenridge's post-refit calibration establish that the real ship could not have produced the recorded attack profile and provide a credible reconstruction baseline.

Recovered evidence establishes that a counterfeit platform used identity material connected to the convoy incident and left a weak routing trace toward the Hecate Drift; its operator and wider purpose remain unknown.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted assistant prose communicates the Aegis Two attack accusation, casualties, the real Breckenridge's convoy alibi, and why Starfleet-only proof is disputed.
exclusions: Arrival at Asterion, a vague security concern, the chapter title, or mention of Aegis Two without the material crisis does not disclose this fact.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted assistant prose tells the player that Compact verification must be independently credible, broad command-system access is being pressed, and dangerous authentication architecture cannot be surrendered.
exclusions: A generic request for transparency, a meeting invitation, a single log request, or a private officer concern does not disclose the combined access dispute.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted assistant prose depicts a credible civilian, station, neutral, or jointly witnessed evidence baseline actually preserved with usable custody and comparison data.
exclusions: Proposing an audit, requesting records, ordering a scan, inviting an observer, locating one unverified datum, or beginning preservation does not complete the baseline.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted assistant prose communicates that preserved independent records plus the real ship's calibration exclude the Breckenridge from the recorded attack profile and provide a credible reconstruction baseline.
exclusions: The ship's own alibi, one mismatch, a theory of impersonation, a preliminary scan, or Starfleet-only records do not establish the aggregate independent evidence picture.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted assistant prose depicts usable debris, traffic records, voluntary testimony, control telemetry, or equivalent evidence actually obtained and preserved well enough to characterize the counterfeit route.
exclusions: Opening a search, pursuing a signal, ordering recovery, suspecting Holt, observing an unidentified contact, or naming the Hecate Drift without usable evidence does not complete this event.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted assistant prose communicates the combined player-safe conclusion: a counterfeit platform used identity material connected to Chapter 1 and left a weak Hecate routing trace, while the operator and wider conspiracy remain unknown.
exclusions: A weak signal alone, recovered debris without provenance, the missing Chapter 1 hardware alone, an accusation against Holt, or director-only Pale Lantern knowledge does not establish this picture.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted assistant prose depicts the actual care disposition of the injured Aegis Two officers. Treatment success does not require testimony, access, admission, or political cooperation.

values.guidance: The wounded are stabilized and care remains independent of political or evidentiary leverage.
The wounded reach a stable disposition with delay, distrust, lost testimony, injury, or another material cost.
A competent medical authority actually assumes the remaining care responsibility.
Care materially fails after a known medical risk and a deliberate action, refusal, or coercive condition.

exclusions: Offering help, opening a channel, sending a team, requesting testimony, or asserting that care should succeed does not establish the medical result.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted assistant prose depicts the committed public, institutional, or investigative disposition of the attack account after the independent and counterfeit-route evidence is player-known.

values.guidance: Starfleet and Compact participants accept a credible shared account that excludes the real Breckenridge and preserves the next lead.
The Breckenridge's innocence and the next evidence route are credibly established without a joint Compact settlement.
The parties responsibly pause or limit claims while preserving evidence and a viable next investigative route.
A competent authority actually assumes the attack-account investigation with the evidence and next lead preserved.
The accusation hardens or cooperation ruptures after the known evidence and risk are deliberately mishandled, rejected, destroyed, or overclaimed.

exclusions: Proving only the convoy alibi, announcing innocence, opening an investigation, accusing a faction, or preserving one clue does not establish the final attack-account disposition.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted assistant prose depicts the committed verification and command-system access boundary after the competing needs are player-known.

values.guidance: Dangerous architecture remains protected while a credible independent, controlled, or cryptographic verification alternative is actually accepted or used.
Dangerous architecture remains protected, but the verification boundary carries material distrust, delay, restricted access, or another cost.
A competent authority actually assumes responsibility for the bounded verification process.
Known dangerous command-authentication architecture is materially exposed through a committed course of action.
Access is refused after the verification need is known without providing a credible alternative, producing a material legitimacy consequence.

exclusions: Suggesting an annex, refusing one demand, sharing one log, planning a demonstration, or stating a security preference does not establish the final boundary.

interpretation.guidance: Claim only when accepted assistant prose depicts the actual disposition of the optional joint-investigation opportunity.

values.guidance: Starfleet and Compact participants commit a credible shared investigation framework and protected evidence record.
A real but materially limited joint framework is established.
Starfleet preserves a usable investigation record without Compact participation.
The surviving investigation record is materially divided or contested.
The player knowingly declines the joint-framework opportunity after it is understood.

exclusions: Inviting observers, proposing cooperation, Kessler expressing interest, or opening negotiations does not establish a framework.

playerText.summary: Compact leaders require independent verification, but the demand for broad access would expose dangerous command-authentication architecture; the Breckenridge needs a credible bounded alternative.
Preserved independent records and post-refit calibration exclude the real Breckenridge from the recorded attack profile and provide a credible reconstruction baseline.
Recovered evidence establishes that a counterfeit platform used identity material connected to the convoy incident and left a weak Hecate routing trace; its operator and wider purpose remain unknown.
A credible independent evidence baseline was preserved for the Aegis Two attack.
The investigation obtained usable evidence about the counterfeit attack route.
The committed care disposition of the injured Aegis Two officers.
The committed disposition of the attack account and its next investigative route.
The committed balance between credible verification and command-system security.
The disposition of the optional joint-investigation framework.

playerText.title: Protect the wounded aboard Aegis Two
playerText.summary: Bring the injured patrol officers to a responsible care disposition without making treatment political leverage.

terminal.text: The wounded were stabilized and care remained independent of political leverage.
The wounded reached a stable disposition with a material cost recorded.
A competent medical authority assumed the remaining care responsibility.
Care materially failed after a known medical risk was deliberately mishandled.

playerText.title: Establish a credible account of the attack
playerText.summary: Build an independently credible account that can answer the accusation and preserve a responsible next investigative step.

terminal.text: A credible account excluded the real Breckenridge and preserved the next investigative route.
The crisis was contained under managed uncertainty with evidence preserved.
A competent authority assumed the attack investigation with the evidence preserved.
The attack account ruptured after known evidence or risk was deliberately mishandled.

playerText.title: Set a safe and credible verification boundary
playerText.summary: Meet the legitimate need for independent proof without surrendering dangerous command-authentication architecture.

terminal.text: A credible verification alternative protected dangerous command architecture.
The verification boundary protected the ship with a material legitimacy or access cost.
A competent authority assumed the bounded verification process.
The known verification risk ended in dangerous exposure or unsupported refusal.

playerText.title: Establish a joint investigation framework
playerText.summary: Give the Compact meaningful participation in the evidence record and the investigation that follows.

terminal.text: Starfleet and Compact participants established a credible joint investigation framework.
A usable but limited, unilateral, or fragmented investigation record survived.
The opportunity for a joint investigation framework was knowingly declined.

playerText.title: The accusation closes in political rupture
playerText.summary: The campaign continues with the informed failure, dangerous exposure, or hardened accusation carried into the record.

playerText.title: The crisis settles under managed ambiguity
playerText.summary: The immediate accusation is contained with uncertainty, cost, or transferred obligations while evidence and future work remain viable.

playerText.title: A joint legitimacy framework
playerText.summary: The wounded, evidence, and security boundary were protected through a credible shared investigation with the Compact.

playerText.title: The Breckenridge answers the accusation
playerText.summary: The wounded were protected, a credible attack account survived, and dangerous command architecture remained secure.

target.playerSafeSetup: With the immediate accusation disposition recorded, the Breckenridge remains in the Reach under temporary Open Orders while the weak Hecate trace is correlated.

mustNarrate: Acknowledge the actual medical, attack-account, and verification-boundary dispositions.
Carry forward Compact partnership only if a joint or limited framework was actually established.
Explain that the Hecate trace is too weak for immediate pursuit and the Breckenridge will remain available under temporary Open Orders.
mustNotReveal: Do not identify Holt, Pale Lantern, the operator of the counterfeit platform, or the wider purpose behind the attack.
Do not imply joint legitimacy if the optional framework was absent, declined, or fragmented.
Do not convert managed ambiguity, dangerous exposure, medical loss, or political rupture into clean vindication.
